   match result {\n333\t        Ok(timestamp) => Ok(timestamp),\n334\t        Err(_) => Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\n335\t            \"chrono operation panicked - possibly due to extreme system clock values\"\n336\t        )),\n337\t    }\n338\t}\n339\t\n340\t/// Parse the backend name from a binary's version output.\n341\t///\n342\t/// Runs the specified binary with the given version command arguments,\n343\t/// captures stdout, and extracts the backend name (first word of output).\n344\t///\n345\t/// This function includes ETXTBSY (errno 26) retry logic to handle the race\n346\t/// condition where a binary written to disk immediately before execution\n347\t/// transiently reports \"Text file busy\".\n348\t///\n349\t/// # Arguments\n350\t///\n351\t/// * `binary_path` - Path to the binary to execute\n352\t/// * `version_args` - Arguments to pass for version check (e.g., `[\"--version\"]`)\n353\t///\n354\t/// # Returns\n355\t///\n356\t/// * `Result<String>` - The extracted backend name, or an error if:\n357\t///   - Binary not found\n358\t///   - Binary exits with non-zero code\n359\t///   - Output is empty or unparseable\n360\t///\n361\t/// # Examples\n362\t///\n363\t/// ```no_run\n364\t/// use needle::util::parse_backend_name_from_version;\n365\t/// use std::path::Path;\n366\t///\n367\t/// # fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> {\n368\t/// let backend = parse_backend_name_from_version(\n369\t///     Path::new(\"/usr/local/bin/bf\"),\n370\t///     &[\"--version\"]\n371\t/// )?;\n372\t/// assert_eq!(backend, \"bf\");\n373\t/// # Ok(())\n374\t/// # }\n375\t/// ```\n376\tpub fn parse_backend_name_from_version(\n377\t    binary_path: &std::path::Path,\n378\t    version_args: &[&str],\n379\t) -> Result<String> {\n380\t    use std::process::{Command, Stdio};\n381\t    use std::thread;\n382\t\n383\t    // Check if binary exists\n384\t    if !binary_path.exists() {\n385\t        anyhow::bail!(\"binary not found at {}\", binary_path.display());\n386\t    }\n387\t\n388\t    // ETXTBSY retry logic: retry with backoff when the kernel reports \"Text file busy\"\n389\t    const ETXTBSY_ERRNO: i32 = 26;\n390\t    let max_attempts = 5;\n391\t    let backoff_ms = 20;\n392\t\n393\t    let mut last_err = None;\n394\t    for attempt in 0..max_attempts {\n395\t        let result = Command::new(binary_path)\n396\t            .args(version_args)\n397\t            .stdout(Stdio::piped())\n398\t            .stderr(Stdio::piped())\n399\t            .output();\n400\t\n401\t        match result {\n402\t            Ok(output) => {\n403\t                if attempt > 0 {\n404\t                    debug!(\n405\t                        attempt = attempt + 1,\n406\t                        max_attempts = max_attempts,\n407\t                        binary = %binary_path.display(),\n408\t                        function = \"parse_backend_name_from_version\",\n409\t                        \"ETXTBSY retry succeeded after {} attempts\",\n410\t                        attempt + 1\n411\t                    );\n412\t                }\n413\t\n414\t                // Check exit status\n415\t                if !output.status.success() {\n416\t                    let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);\n417\t                    anyhow::bail!(\n418\t                        \"binary {} exited with code {}: {}\",\n419\t                        binary_path.display(),\n420\t                        output.status.code().unwrap_or(-1),\n421\t                        stderr.trim()\n422\t                    );\n423\t                }\n424\t\n425\t                // Capture stdout\n426\t                let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);\n427\t                let trimmed_output = stdout.trim();\n428\t\n429\t                // Extract backend name (first word)\n430\t                let backend_name = trimmed_output.split_whitespace().next().ok_or_else(|| {\n431\t                    anyhow::anyhow!(\n432\t                        \"binary {} produced empty or unparseable version output\",\n433\t                        binary_path.display()\n434\t                    )\n435\t                })?;\n436\t\n437\t                return Ok(backend_name.to_string());\n438\t            }\n439\t            Err(e) if e.raw_os_error() == Some(ETXTBSY_ERRNO) && attempt + 1 < max_attempts => {\n440\t                last_err = Some(e);\n441\t                warn!(\n442\t                    attempt = attempt + 1,\n443\t                    max_attempts = max_attempts,\n444\t                    backoff_ms = backoff_ms,\n445\t                    binary = %binary_path.display(),\n446\t                    function = \"parse_backend_name_from_version\",\n447\t                    \"ETXTBSY error detected (attempt {}/{}), retrying in {}ms\",\n448\t                    attempt + 1,\n449\t                    max_attempts,\n450\t                    backoff_ms\n451\t                );\n452\t                thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(backoff_ms));\n453\t            }\n454\t            Err(e) => {\n455\t                return Err(e).with_context(|| {\n456\t                    format!(\n457\t                        \"failed to execute binary {} with version args {:?}\",\n458\t                        binary_path.display(),\n459\t                        version_args\n460\t                    )\n461\t                })\n462\t            }\n463\t        }\n464\t    }\n465\t\n466\t    // All retries exhausted\n467\t    Err(last_err.expect(\"loop always sets last_err before exhausting max_attempts\")).with_context(\n468\t        || {\n469\t            format!(\n470\t                \"failed to execute binary {} after {} attempts (ETXTBSY)\",\n471\t                binary_path.display(),\n472\t                max_attempts\n473\t            )\n474\t        },\n475\t    )\n476\t}\n477\t\n478\t/// Crate-wide test-only environment isolation.\n479\t///\n480\t/// `HOME` is process-global, but Rust runs unit tests as threads inside a\n481\t/// single process. Any test that calls `set_var(\"HOME\", ..)` or\n482\t/// `remove_var(\"HOME\")` therefore mutates state that every concurrently\n483\t/// running test observes. Before this module existed, several modules each\n484\t/// had their own private `Mutex` (or none at all), which provides no mutual\n485\t/// exclusion against the others — tests that merely *read* `HOME`\n486\t/// (`worker::tests`, `telemetry::tests`, tilde expansion) failed\n487\t/// nondeterministically depending on interleaving.\n488\t///\n489\t/// Every test that reads or writes `HOME`/`PATH` must go through\n490\t/// [`isolate_env`] or [`isolate_env_with_home`] so that exactly one such test\n491\t/// runs at a time and the previous values are always restored.\n492\t#[cfg(test)]\n493\tpub(crate) mod test_env {\n494\t    use std::ffi::OsString;\n495\t    use std::sync::{Mutex, MutexGuard};\n496\t\n497\t    /// The single process-wide lock guarding `HOME`/`PATH` in tests.\n498\t    static ENV_LOCK: Mutex<()> = Mutex::new(());\n499\t\n500\t    /// Variables guarded by [`isolate_env`].\n501\t    ///\n502\t    /// Concurrent `set_var` corrupts the process environment for every\n503\t    /// thread — including `Command` spawns reading `PATH`, which is how an\n504\t    /// unrelated test's `git` invocation dies with `NotFound` while some\n505\t    /// other test mutates an env var (observed in CI: needle-ci-wbgtb,\n506\t    /// commit_hook::concurrent_inject_never_cross_tags). Any test mutating\n507\t    /// one of these must hold the lock for its whole body.\n508\t    const GUARDED_VARS: [&str; 5] = [\n509\t        \"HOME\",\n510\t        \"PATH\",\n511\t        \"NEEDLE_HOME\",\n512\t        \"NEEDLE_EVENTS\",\n513\t        \"NEEDLE_HEARTBEATS\",\n514\t    ];\n515\t\n516\t    /// Restores every guarded variable to its captured value when dropped.\n517\t    pub(crate) struct EnvGuard {\n518\t        saved: Vec<(&'static str, Option<OsString>)>,\n519\t    }\n520\t\n521\t    impl Drop for EnvGuard {\n522\t        fn drop(&mut self) {\n523\t            for (key, value) in self.saved.drain(..) {\n524\t                restore(key, value);\n525\t            }\n526\t        }\n527\t    }\n528\t\n529\t    fn restore(key: &str, value: Option<OsString>) {\n530\t        match value {\n531\t            Some(value) => std::env::set_var(key, value),\n532\t            None => std::env::remove_var(key),\n533\t        }\n534\t    }\n535\t\n536\t    /// A private, per-caller NEEDLE home for tests.\n537\t    ///\n538\t    /// `WorkspaceConfig::default_home()` resolves to the operator's real\n539\t    /// `~/.needle`, whose `state/workers.json` is the *live fleet's* worker\n540\t    /// registry. Unit tests that construct a `Worker` therefore registered\n541\t    /// themselves into it and raced each other (and the running fleet) on a\n542\t    /// single read-modify-write file. Every test config must point somewhere\n543\t    /// private instead.\n544\t    ///\n545\t    /// Each call returns a fresh subdirectory, so concurrently running tests\n546\t    /// that share a worker id never touch the same registry file. The backing\n547\t    /// root is held in a `OnceLock` for the lifetime of the test process.\n548\t    pub(crate) fn isolated_home() -> std::path::PathBuf {\n549\t        use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};\n550\t        use std::sync::OnceLock;\n551\t\n552\t        static ROOT: OnceLock<tempfile::TempDir> = OnceLock::new();\n553\t        static NEXT: AtomicUsize = AtomicUsize::new(0);\n554\t\n555\t        let root =\n556\t            ROOT.get_or_init(|| tempfile::tempdir().expect(\"failed to create test home root\"));\n557\t        let dir = root\n558\t            .path()\n559\t            .join(format!(\"home-{}\", NEXT.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed)));\n560\t        std::fs::create_dir_all(dir.join(\"state\")).expect(\"failed to create test home state dir\");\n561\t        dir\n562\t    }\n563\t\n564\t    /// Acquire the environment lock and capture `HOME`/`PATH` for restoration.\n565\t    ///\n566\t    /// Hold the returned tuple for the whole test body; dropping it releases\n567\t    /// the lock and restores the environment. The lock is intentionally\n568\t    /// poison-tolerant: a panicking test must not wedge every later test.\n569\t    pub(crate) fn isolate_env() -> (MutexGuard<'static, ()>, EnvGuard) {\n570\t        let lock = ENV_LOCK\n571\t            .lock()\n572\t            .unwrap_or_else(|poisoned| poisoned.into_inner());\n573\t        let guard = EnvGuard {\n574\t            saved: GUARDED_VARS\n575\t                .iter()\n576\t                .map(|&key| (key, std::env::var_os(key)))\n577\t                .collect(),\n578\t        };\n579\t        (lock, guard)\n580\t    }\n581\t}\n582\t\n583\t#[cfg(test)]\n584\tmod tests {\n585\t    use super::*;\n586\t    use chrono::{Datelike, Timelike};\n587\t    use std::env;\n588\t    use std::path::PathBuf;\n589\t\n590\t (\n370\t        \"0.1.\",\n371\t        \"pre-0.2.0 versions have truncation bugs with default limits\",\n372\t    ),\n373\t];\n374\t\n375\t// ─── ETXTBSY retry helper ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n376\t\n377\t/// Retry wrapper for subprocess spawns that handle ETXTBSY (errno 26).\n378\t///\n379\t/// ETXTBSY (\"Text file busy\") occurs when the kernel blocks execution of a binary\n380\t/// that has a write-mode file descriptor still open. This is a genuine race condition:\n381\t///\n382\t/// 1. A process writes a binary to disk and closes the file descriptor.\n383\t/// 2. The kernel's page cache and filesystem synchronization haven't fully completed.\n384\t/// 3. Another process immediately attempts to `exec()` the same binary.\n385\t/// 4. The kernel returns ETXTBSY (errno 26) because the file is still marked for write.\n386\t///\n387\t/// This is most common with:\n388\t/// - Freshly-extracted upgrade binaries executed immediately\n389\t/// - Test fixtures written and chmod'd immediately before use\n390\t/// - Any binary that's written to disk and executed in quick succession\n391\t///\n392\t/// The race is narrow (typically <100ms) but real. Retrying with a short backoff\n393\t/// is the correct fix — the file descriptor is already closed, we're just waiting\n394\t/// for the kernel to finish its internal bookkeeping.\n395\t///\n396\t/// # Parameters\n397\t///\n398\t/// * `spawn_fn` - An async function that attempts to spawn the subprocess\n399\t/// * `max_attempts` - Maximum number of retry attempts (default: 5)\n400\t/// * `backoff_ms` - Backoff delay between retries in milliseconds (default: 20)\n401\t///\n402\t/// # Returns\n403\t///\n404\t/// * `Ok(T)` - The subprocess output on success\n405\t/// * `Err(io::Error)` - The last error if all attempts are exhausted\n406\t///\n407\t/// # When to use this helper\n408\t///\n409\t/// Use this wrapper whenever spawning a subprocess that may have been written to\n410\t/// disk immediately before execution:\n411\t///\n412\t/// - Freshly-installed or updated binaries\n413\t/// - Test fixtures created during test setup\n414\t/// - Any executable extracted from an archive and immediately run\n415\t///\n416\t/// Do NOT use this for long-running processes or stable system binaries — the\n417\t/// retry overhead is unnecessary and ETXTBSY is unlikely in those cases.\n418\t///\n419\t/// # Example\n420\t///\n421\t/// ```no_run\n422\t/// use std::path::Path;\n423\t/// use needle::bead_store::spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry;\n424\t///\n425\t/// # async fn example() -> Result<(), std::io::Error> {\n426\t/// let binary_path = Path::new(\"/path/to/binary\");\n427\t/// let output = spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry(\n428\t///     || async {\n429\t///         tokio::process::Command::new(binary_path)\n430\t///             .arg(\"--version\")\n431\t///             .output()\n432\t///             .await\n433\t///     },\n434\t///     5,\n435\t///     20,\n436\t/// ).await?;\n437\t/// # Ok(())\n438\t/// # }\n439\t/// ```\n440\tpub async fn spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry<F, Fut, T>(\n441\t    spawn_fn: F,\n442\t    max_attempts: u32,\n443\t    backoff_ms: u64,\n444\t) -> std::io::Result<T>\n445\twhere\n446\t    F: Fn() -> Fut,\n447\t    Fut: std::future::Future<Output = std::io::Result<T>>,\n448\t{\n449\t    let mut last_err = None;\n450\t    for attempt in 0..max_attempts {\n451\t        match spawn_fn().await {\n452\t            Ok(output) => {\n453\t                if attempt > 0 {\n454\t                    debug!(\n455\t                        attempt = attempt + 1,\n456\t                        max_attempts = max_attempts,\n457\t                        function = \"spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry\",\n458\t                        \"ETXTBSY retry succeeded after {} attempts\",\n459\t                        attempt + 1\n460\t                    );\n461\t                }\n462\t                return Ok(output);\n463\t            }\n464\t            Err(e) if e.raw_os_error() == Some(26) && attempt + 1 < max_attempts => {\n465\t                last_err = Some(e);\n466\t                warn!(\n467\t                    attempt = attempt + 1,\n468\t                    max_attempts = max_attempts,\n469\t                    backoff_ms = backoff_ms,\n470\t                    function = \"spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry\",\n471\t                    \"ETXTBSY error detected (attempt {}/{}), retrying in {}ms\",\n472\t                    attempt + 1,\n473\t                    max_attempts,\n474\t                    backoff_ms\n475\t                );\n476\t                tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(backoff_ms)).await;\n477\t            }\n478\t            Err(e) => return Err(e),\n479\t        }\n480\t    }\n481\t    Err(last_err.expect(\"loop always sets last_err before exhausting MAX_ATTEMPTS\"))\n482\t}\n483\t\n484\t/// Retry wrapper for `Command::spawn()` calls that handle ETXTBSY (errno 26).\n485\t///\n486\t/// Specialized version of `spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry` for subprocess spawns that\n487\t/// return a `Child` process. Use this when you need to interact with the spawned\n488\t/// process (e.g., for timeout handling with `kill_on_drop`).\n489\t///\n490\t/// # Parameters\n491\t///\n492\t/// * `spawn_fn` - An async function that attempts to spawn the subprocess\n493\t/// * `max_attempts` - Maximum number of retry attempts (default: 5)\n494\t/// * `backoff_ms` - Backoff delay between retries in milliseconds (default: 20)\n495\t///\n496\t/// # Returns\n497\t///\n498\t/// * `Ok(Child)` - The spawned child process on success\n499\t/// * `Err(io::Error)` - The last error if all attempts are exhausted\n500\tpub async fn spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_child<F, Fut>(\n501\t    spawn_fn: F,\n502\t    max_attempts: u32,\n503\t    backoff_ms: u64,\n504\t) -> std::io::Result<tokio::process::Child>\n505\twhere\n506\t    F: Fn() -> Fut,\n507\t    Fut: std::future::Future<Output = std::io::Result<tokio::process::Child>>,\n508\t{\n509\t    spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry(spawn_fn, max_attempts, backoff_ms).await\n510\t}\n511\t\n512\t/// Retry wrapper for subprocess spawns with exponential backoff for ETXTBSY (errno 26).\n513\t///\n514\t/// This variant uses **exponential backoff** with jitter, making it more suitable for\n515\t/// high-concurrency scenarios where multiple processes might race for the same binary.\n516\t/// Exponential backoff prevents thundering herd problems that linear backoff can cause.\n517\t///\n518\t/// The backoff formula is: `base_ms * 2^attempt + random_jitter`, where:\n519\t/// - `base_ms` is the initial delay (default: 20ms)\n520\t/// - `attempt` is the current retry number (0-indexed)\n521\t/// - `random_jitter` is ±25% of the calculated delay to prevent synchronization\n522\t///\n523\t/// Example backoff sequence with base_ms=20:\n524\t/// - Attempt 1: ~20ms (15-25ms with jitter)\n525\t/// - Attempt 2: ~40ms (30-50ms with jitter)\n526\t/// - Attempt 3: ~80ms (60-100ms with jitter)\n527\t/// - Attempt 4: ~160ms (120-200ms with jitter)\n528\t/// - Attempt 5: ~320ms (240-400ms with jitter)\n529\t///\n530\t/// # Parameters\n531\t///\n532\t/// * `spawn_fn` - An async function that attempts to spawn the subprocess\n533\t/// * `max_attempts` - Maximum number of retry attempts (default: 10)\n534\t/// * `base_ms` - Base backoff delay in milliseconds (default: 20)\n535\t///\n536\t/// # Returns\n537\t///\n538\t/// * `Ok(T)` - The subprocess output on success\n539\t/// * `Err(io::Error)` - The last error if all attempts are exhausted\n540\t///\n541\t/// # When to use exponential vs linear backoff\n542\t///\n543\t/// Use exponential backoff when:\n544\t/// - Spawning multiple processes concurrently that might race for the same binary\n545\t/// - Running in high-concurrency environments (CI, parallel tests)\n546\t/// - Dealing with slow filesystems where the race window might be longer\n547\t///\n548\t/// Use linear backoff (`spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry`) when:\n549\t/// - Spawning a single process in isolation\n550\t/// - The race window is known to be very short (<50ms)\n551\t/// - Minimal latency is more important than thundering herd prevention\n552\t///\n553\t/// # Example\n554\t///\n555\t/// ```no_run\n556\t/// use std::path::Path;\n557\t/// use needle::bead_store::spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential;\n558\t///\n559\t/// # async fn example() -> Result<(), std::io::Error> {\n560\t/// let binary_path = Path::new(\"/path/to/freshly-written-binary\");\n561\t/// let output = spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential(\n562\t///     || async {\n563\t///         tokio::process::Command::new(binary_path)\n564\t///             .arg(\"--version\")\n565\t///             .output()\n566\t///             .await\n567\t///     },\n568\t///     10,\n569\t///     20,\n570\t/// ).await?;\n571\t/// # Ok(())\n572\t/// # }\n573\t/// ```\n574\tpub async fn spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential<F, Fut, T>(\n575\t    spawn_fn: F,\n576\t    max_attempts: u32,\n577\t    base_ms: u64,\n578\t) -> std::io::Result<T>\n579\twhere\n580\t    F: Fn() -> Fut,\n581\t    Fut: std::future::Future<Output = std::io::Result<T>>,\n582\t{\n583\t    use rand::Rng;\n584\t\n585\t    const ETXTBSY_ERRNO: i32 = 26;\n586\t    const JITTER_PERCENT: f64 = 0.25; // ±25% jitter\n587\t\n588\t    let mut last_err = None;\n589\t    let mut rng = rand::thread_rng();\n590\t\n591\t    for attempt in 0..max_attempts {\n592\t        match spawn_fn().await {\n593\t            Ok(output) => {\n594\t                if attempt > 0 {\n595\t                    debug!(\n596\t                        attempt = attempt + 1,\n597\t                        max_attempts = max_attempts,\n598\t                        function = \"spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential\",\n599\t                        \"ETXTBSY exponential retry succeeded after {} attempts\",\n600\t                        attempt + 1\n601\t                    );\n602\t                }\n603\t                return Ok(output);\n604\t            }\n605\t            Err(e) if e.raw_os_error() == Some(ETXTBSY_ERRNO) && attempt + 1 < max_attempts => {\n606\t                last_err = Some(e);\n607\t\n608\t                // Calculate exponential backoff: base_ms * 2^attempt\n609\t                let exponential_delay = base_ms * (1 << attempt);\n610\t\n611\t                // Add jitter to prevent synchronization\n612\t                let jitter_range = (exponential_delay as f64 * JITTER_PERCENT) as u64;\n613\t                let jitter = rng.gen_range(0..=jitter_range * 2);\n614\t                let delay = exponential_delay\n615\t                    .saturating_add(jitter)\n616\t                    .saturating_sub(jitter_range);\n617\t\n618\t                warn!(\n619\t                    attempt = attempt + 1,\n620\t                    max_attempts = max_attempts,\n621\t                    delay_ms = delay,\n622\t                    function = \"spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential\",\n623\t                    \"ETXTBSY error detected (attempt {}/{}), retrying in ~{}ms (exponential backoff with jitter)\",\n624\t                    attempt + 1,\n625\t                    max_attempts,\n626\t                    delay\n627\t                );\n628\t                tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(delay)).await;\n629\t            }\n630\t            Err(e) => return Err(e),\n631\t        }\n632\t    }\n633\t\n634\t    Err(last_err.expect(\"loop always sets last_err before exhausting max_attempts\"))\n635\t}\n636\t\n637\t/// Retry wrapper for `Command::spawn()` with exponential backoff for ETXTBSY (errno 26).\n638\t///\n639\t/// Specialized version of spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync_exponential<F, T>(\n770\t    spawn_fn: F,\n771\t    max_attempts: u32,\n772\t    base_ms: u64,\n773\t) -> std::io::Result<T>\n774\twhere\n775\t    F: Fn() -> std::io::Result<T>,\n776\t{\n777\t    use rand::Rng;\n778\t\n779\t    const ETXTBSY_ERRNO: i32 = 26;\n780\t    const JITTER_PERCENT: f64 = 0.25; // ±25% jitter\n781\t\n782\t    let mut last_err = None;\n783\t    let mut rng = rand::thread_rng();\n784\t\n785\t    for attempt in 0..max_attempts {\n786\t        match spawn_fn() {\n787\t            Ok(output) => {\n788\t                if attempt \"spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync_exponential\",\n793\t                        \"ETXTBSY sync exponential retry succeeded after {} attempts\",\n794\t                        attempt + 1\n795\t {\n800\t                last_err = Some(e);\n801\t\n802\t                // Calculate exponential backoff: base_ms * 2^attempt\n803\t                let exponential_delay = base_ms * (1 << attempt);\n804\t\n805\t                // Add jitter to prevent synchronization\n806\t                let jitter_range = (exponential_delay as f64 * JITTER_PERCENT) as u64;\n807\t                let jitter = rng.gen_range(0..=jitter_range * 2);\n808\t                let delay = exponential_delay\n809\t                    .saturating_add(jitter)\n810\t backoff with jitter)\",\n818\t                    attempt + 1,\n819\t                    max_attempts,\n820\t                    delay\n821\t                );\n822\t always sets last_err before exhausting max_attempts\"))\n829\t}\n830\t\n831\t/// Synchronous retry wrapper for `Command::spawn()` with exponential backoff for ETXTBSY (errno 26).\n832\t///\n833\t/// outcomes_match(&self, expected: &ExpectedOutcome, actual: &ActualOutcome) -> bool {\n691\t        match expected {\n692\t            ExpectedOutcome::Success {\n693\t }\n782\t\n783\t    /// Promote :testing to :stable, backing up the current :stable.\n784\t    ///\n785\t    /// This operation is atomic at the filesystem level:\n786\t    /// 1. Move :stable to :stable.prev\n787\t    /// 2. Move :testing to :stable\n788\t    /// 3. Update symlink\n789\t    pub fn promote(&self) -> Result<()> {\n790\t        let testing = self.testing_binary();\n791\t        let stable = self.stable_binary();\n792\t        let prev = self.prev_binary();\n793\t        let symlink = self.symlink_path();\n794\t\n795\t        if !testing.exists() {\n796\t            bail!(\"testing binary not found: {}\", testing.display());\n797\t        }\n798\t\n799\t        // Ensure bin directory exists.\n800\t        let bin_dir = self.needle_home.join(\"bin\");\n801\t        std::fs::create_dir_all(&bin_dir).context(\"failed to create bin backup\")?;\n806\t        }\n807\t\n808\t        // Step 2: Move current stable to backup (if exists).\n809\t        if stable.exists() {\n810\t            std::fs::rename(&stable, &prev).context(\"failed to backup stable binary\")?;\n811\t        }\n812\t\n813\t        // Step 3: Move testing to stable.\n814\t        std::fs::rename(&testing, &stable).context(\"failed to promote testing to stable\")?;\n815\t\n816\t        // Step 4: Update symlink.\n817\t        if symlink.exists() || symlink.is_symlink() {\n818\t create symlink\")?;\n822\t        #[cfg(not(unix))]\n823\t        {\n824\t            // Fallback: copy instead of symlink on non-Unix.\n825\t            std::fs::copy(&stable, &symlink).context(\"failed to copy stable to symlink\")?;\n826\t        }\n827\t\n828\t        tracing::info!(\n829\t            testing = %testing.display(),\n830\t            stable = %stable.display(),\n831\t            prev = %prev.display(),\n832\t            symlink = %symlink.display(),\n833\t            \"promoted testing to stable\"\n834\t        );\n835\t\n836\t        Ok(())\n837\t    }\n838\t\n839\t    /// Reject :testing (discard without promoting).\n840\t    ///\n841\t    /// The fleet remains on :stable unchanged.\n842\t    pub fn reject(&self) -> Result<()>        Ok(())\n853\t    }\n854\t\n855\t    /// Rollback to the previous stable binary.\n856\t    ///\n857\t    /// Restores :stable.prev as :stable.\n858\t    pub fn rollback(&self) -> Result<()> {\n859\t        let stable = self.stable_binary();\n860\t        let prev = self.prev_binary();\n861\t        let symlink = self.symlink_path();\n862\t\n863\t        if !prev.exists() {\n864\t the lifetime of the supervisor daemon.\n1146\t///\n1147\t/// Safe to call unconditionally every tick: `needle supervise` only ever\n1148\t/// directly spawns worker processes — gate commands and dispatch\n1149\t/// subprocesses are spawned by the *worker* process, a separate PID tree —\n1150\t/// so a blind `waitpid(-1, ...)` here cannot race with `.wait()` calls\n1151\t/// elsewhere in the codebase (`dispatch`/`telemetry`/`canary`), which all\n1152\t/// run in different processes. See ADR-010 / GH #12.\n1153\t#[cfg(unix)]\n1154\tfn reap_zombie_children() {\n1155\t    reap_children_matching(-1);\n1156\t}\n1157\t\n1158\t#[cfg(not(unix))]\n1159\tfn reap_zombie_children() {}\n1160\t\n1161\t/// Shared implementation of the `WNOHANG` reap loop, parameterized by which\n1162\t/// PID to wait on (`-1` in production, meaning \"any direct child\" — see\n1163\t/// `reap_zombie_children`). Split out so tests can exercise the exact same\n1164\t/// loop scoped to a single PID they spawned themselves, instead of calling\n1165\t/// the crate-wide `-1` sweep from inside the shared `cargo test --lib`\n1166\t/// process, where it could reap an unrelated concurrently-running test's own\n1167\t/// child (unit tests across the whole crate share one process/many threads,\n1168\t/// unlike separate integration-test binaries).\n1169\t#[cfg(unix)]\n1170\tfn reap_children_matching(target_pid: libc::pid_t) {\n1171\t    loop {\n1172\t        let mut status: libc::c_int = 0;\n1173\t        // SAFETY: waitpid(target_pid, &mut status, WNOHANG) reaps an\n1174\t        // already-exited child (any direct child, if target_pid == -1)\n1175\t        // without blocking; `status` is a valid stack-local out parameter\n1176\t        // for the duration of the call.\n1177\t        let pid = unsafe { libc::waitpid(target_pid, &mut status, libc::WNOHANG) };\n1178\t        match pid {\n1179\t            0 => break,          // No exited children ready to reap right now.\n1180\t            n if n < 0 => break, // ECHILD (no children) or another errno; stop for this tick.\n1181\t            n => tracing::debug!(reaped_pid = n, \"reaped exited worker child\"),\n1182\t        }\n1183\t    }\n1184\t}\n1185\t\n1186\t/// Run the supervisor from the CLI.\n1187\t///\n1188\t/// This is the entry The heartbeat file - if it exists and is recent, a supervisor is active\n1228\t/// 2. path.exists()\n1324\t}\n1325\t\n1326\t// ─── Tests ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n1327\t\n1328\t#[cfg(test)]\n1329\tmod tests {\n1330\t    use ──\n1719\t\n1720\t    #[cfg(unix)]\n1721\t    #[test]\n1722\t    fn reap_zombie_children_reaps_an_exited_child() {\n1723\t        // Exercises reap_children_matching (the exact loop reap_zombie_children\n1724\t        // wraps) scoped to a PID we spawned ourselves — NOT the real\n1725\t        // reap_zombie_children()'s `-1` (any child) target. Unit tests across\n1726\t        // the whole crate share one process/many threads under `cargo test\n1727\t        // --lib`; calling the `-1` sweep here could reap an unrelated,\n1728\t        // concurrently-running test's own child out from under it. Scoping to\n1729\t        // our own PID exercises the identical waitpid/WNOHANG logic with none\n1730\t        // of that collision risk.\n1731\t        //\n1732\t        // Spawn a real short-lived child directly (no setsid/detach — this\n1733\t        // test process is its real parent).\n1734\t        let child = std::process::Command::new(\"true\")\n1735\t            .spawn()\n1736\t            .expect(\"failed to spawn `true`\");\n1737\t        let pid = child.id();\n1738\t\n1739\t        // Wait for it to actually exit (without reaping it — do not call\n1740\t        // child.wait() here, that would reap it ourselves and defeat the test).\n1741\t        let stat_path = format!(\"/proc/{pid}/stat\");\n1742\t        let mut became_zombie = false;\n1743\t        for _ in 0..200 {\n1744\t            if let Ok(stat) = std::fs::read_to_string(&stat_path) {\n1745\t                if let Some(after_comm) = stat.rfind(')') {\n1746\t                    if stat[after_comm + 1..].trim_start().starts_with('Z') {\n1747\t                        became_zombie = true;\n1748\t                        break;\n1749\t                    }\n1750\t                }\n1751\t            } else {\n1752\t                // Already reaped by something else, or /proc entry gone —\n1753\t                // can't validate the pre-condition; skip rather than false-fail.\n1754\t                break;\n1755\t            }\n1756\t            std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(10));\n1757\t        }\n1758\t        assert!(\n1759\t            became_zombie,\n1760\t            \"child did not reach zombie state before timeout — test precondition not met\"\n1761\t        );\n1762\t\n1763\t        reap_children_matching(pid as libc::pid_t);\n1764\t\n1765\t        // After reaping, /proc/<pid> should no longer exist.\n1766\t        assert!(\n1767\t            !std::path::Path::new(&stat_path).exists(),\n1768\t            \"child was not reaped: {stat_path} still exists\"\n1769\t        );\n1770\t\n1771\t        // Prevent a double-wait/drop warning: the child is already reaped by\n1772\t        // our sweep, so explicitly forget rather than calling child.wait().\n1773\t        std::mem::forget(child);\n1774\t    }\n1775\t\n1776\t    // ── Supervisor startup resolved path logging test (bf-5hnpy) ──\n1777\t\n1778\t    #[tokio::test]\n1779\t processes concurrently that might race for the same binary\\n545\\t/// - Running in high-concurrency environments (CI, parallel tests)\\n546\\t/// - Dealing with slow filesystems where the race window {\\n1266\\t        return Ok(true);\\n1267\\t    }\\n1268\\t\\n1269\\t    // Fall back to socket check if configured\\n1270\\t    if let Some(socket) = socket_path {\\n1271\\t        return Ok(socket_exists(socket));\\n1272\\t    }\\n1273\\t\\n1274\\t    Ok(false)\\n1275\\t}\\n1276\\t\\n1277\\t/// Check if the heartbeat file exists and was modified recently.\\n1278\\t///\\n1279\\t/// A heartbeat is considered \\\"recent\\\" if it was modified within the last 30 seconds.\\n1280\\t/// This threshold accounts for supervisor heartbeat intervals and clock skew.\\n1281\\t///\\n1282\\t/// # Arguments\\n1283\\t///\\n1284\\t/// * `path` - Path to the heartbeat file\\n1285\\t///\\n1286\\t/// # Returns\\n1287\\t///\\n1288\\t/// * `Ok(true)` if the file exists and was modified within 30 seconds\\n1289\\t/// * `Ok(false)` if the file doesn't exist or is stale\\n1290\\t/// * `Err(e)` if filesystem access fails\\n1291\\tfn heartbeat_exists_and_is_recent(path: &Path) -> Result<bool> {\\n1292\\t    use std::time::{SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};\\n1293\\t\\n1294\\t    let metadata = match std::fs::metadata(path) {\\n1295\\t        Ok(m) => m,\\n1296\\t        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Ok(false),\\n1297\\t        Err(e) => return Err(e.into()),\\n1298\\t    };\\n1299\\t\\n1300\\t    let modified = metadata.modified()?;\\n1301\\t    let now = SystemTime::now();\\n1302\\t    let elapsed = now.duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH).unwrap().as_secs()\\n1303\\t        - modified.duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH).unwrap().as_secs();\\n1304\\t\\n1305\\t    // Heartbeat is recent if modified within 30 seconds\\n1306\\t    Ok(elapsed <= 30)\\n1307\\t}\\n1308\\t\\n1309\\t/// Check if a socket file exists.\\n1310\\t///\\n1311\\t/// Unix domain sockets appear as files in the filesystem. This function checks\\n1312\\t/// for the socket's existence without attempting to connect.\\n1313\\t///\\n1314\\t/// # Arguments\\n1315\\t///\\n1316\\t/// * `path` - Path to the socket file\\n1317\\t///\\n1318\\t/// # Returns\\n1319\\t///\\n1320\\t/// * `true` if the socket file exists\\n1321\\t/// * `false` otherwise\\n1322\\tfn socket_exists(path: &Path) -> bool {\\n1323\\t    path.exists()\\n1324\\t}\\n1325\\t\\n1326\\t// ─── Tests ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\\n1327\\t\\n1328\\t#[cfg(test)]\\n1329\\tmod tests {\\n1330\\t    use processes concurrently that might race for the same binary\\n545\\t/// - Running in high-concurrency environments (CI, parallel tests)\\n546\\t/// - Dealing with slow filesystems where the race window {\\n1266\\t        return Ok(true);\\n1267\\t    }\\n1268\\t\\n1269\\t    // Fall back to socket check if configured\\n1270\\t    if let Some(socket) = socket_path {\\n1271\\t        return Ok(socket_exists(socket));\\n1272\\t    }\\n1273\\t\\n1274\\t    Ok(false)\\n1275\\t}\\n1276\\t\\n1277\\t/// Check if the heartbeat file exists and was modified recently.\\n1278\\t///\\n1279\\t/// A heartbeat is considered \\\"recent\\\" if it was modified within the last 30 seconds.\\n1280\\t/// This threshold accounts for supervisor heartbeat intervals and clock skew.\\n1281\\t///\\n1282\\t/// # Arguments\\n1283\\t///\\n1284\\t/// * `path` - Path to the heartbeat file\\n1285\\t///\\n1286\\t/// # Returns\\n1287\\t///\\n1288\\t/// * `Ok(true)` if the file exists and was modified within 30 seconds\\n1289\\t/// * `Ok(false)` if the file doesn't exist or is stale\\n1290\\t/// * `Err(e)` if filesystem access fails\\n1291\\tfn heartbeat_exists_and_is_recent(path: &Path) -> Result<bool> {\\n1292\\t    use std::time::{SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};\\n1293\\t\\n1294\\t    let metadata = match std::fs::metadata(path) {\\n1295\\t        Ok(m) => m,\\n1296\\t        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Ok(false),\\n1297\\t        Err(e) => return Err(e.into()),\\n1298\\t    };\\n1299\\t\\n1300\\t    let modified = metadata.modified()?;\\n1301\\t    let now = SystemTime::now();\\n1302\\t    let elapsed = now.duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH).unwrap().as_secs()\\n1303\\t        - modified.duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH).unwrap().as_secs();\\n1304\\t\\n1305\\t    // Heartbeat is recent if modified within 30 seconds\\n1306\\t    Ok(elapsed <= 30)\\n1307\\t}\\n1308\\t\\n1309\\t/// Check if a socket file exists.\\n1310\\t///\\n1311\\t/// Unix domain sockets appear as files in the filesystem. This function checks\\n1312\\t/// for the socket's existence without attempting to connect.\\n1313\\t///\\n1314\\t/// # Arguments\\n1315\\t///\\n1316\\t/// * `path` - Path to the socket file\\n1317\\t///\\n1318\\t/// # Returns\\n1319\\t///\\n1320\\t/// * `true` if the socket file exists\\n1321\\t/// * `false` otherwise\\n1322\\tfn socket_exists(path: &Path) -> bool {\\n1323\\t    path.exists()\\n1324\\t}\\n1325\\t\\n1326\\t// ─── Tests ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\\n1327\\t\\n1328\\t#[cfg(test)]\\n1329\\tmod tests {\\n1330\\t    use
